For no other faculty or power was made manifest to them by which it might disclose or recount the manner of their origin — how they came to be. However, from the moment when evil stirred itself from within its own nature and rose up in assault against divine wisdom [GAP-25], intending that it might come and usurp dominion over the realm of those who live from the Divine. *That is: the origin of evil and its hells is inscrutable even to itself; it possessed no self-reflective intelligence. It generated from itself [GAP-59: the five fundamental evils of its nature]; which [GAP-60: are] the obscurity of the understanding arising from self-love (smoke), the consuming fire of self-love and its lusts (fire), the persuasive force of reasoning from falsity (wind), falsity itself in its fluid and pervasive form (water), and the total privation of all good and truth (Darkness). From these, false perceptions arise like trees from soil, and innumerable evil affections breed in the depths, each devouring the other in perpetual combat, for evil is never at peace with itself.*

It conspired to wage spiritual combat [GAP-74] against the celestial kingdom and the [GAP-75] supreme Divine order. *That is: the dominant evil, having consolidated all hells under itself, turned its predatory awareness toward heaven, perceiving the quality of divine good and truth, and resolved upon total war against it.*

**¶11:** However, He — the Divine Itself, the Father of Immeasurable [GAP-76: Love and Wisdom] — He also knew [GAP-77] of the impending assault, that it sought to disturb the [GAP-78: realm of] divine wisdom [GAP-79] yet in the providence of His [GAP-80] infinite [GAP-81] He transformed His own proceeding against it [GAP-82] to meet it and overcome it. *That is: the Infinite Divine, perceiving the assault from the hells, did not act by sheer omnipotence — which would have annihilated the freedom upon which all spiritual life depends — but transformed Himself, accommodating His power through wisdom, descending through mediating forms to engage evil on its own ground.*

**¶12:** Indeed, at that time [GAP-83] to proceed against [GAP-84] the Divine [GAP-85]. *The fragment is too sparse for confident translation; the spiritual sense requires that this describes the moment of decision — either the hells' advance against the Divine or the Divine's counter-proceeding.*

**¶13:** [GAP-86: Fr]om its own [GAP-87] it poured itself out [GAP-88] into the fundamental evils: into the obscurity of understanding, the fire of self-love, the force of false persuasion, the flowing falsity, and the total privation. It rose up from the [GAP-89: immense] depth of hell, establishing itself within the false perceptions [GAP-90] arrayed against the Divine. *That is: evil diffused its nature through every mode of spiritual corruption and ascended from the deepest hells, taking root in every false perception as in trees growing upward to challenge heaven.*

**¶14:** Also, at the time when evil generated itself further [GAP-91] it produced its characteristic works — still being established within those works as their animating will. Then the five exterior truths were summoned — the proceeding faculties of the Divine Human. *That is: when evil bore its fruits — its deeds and effects in the world — the Lord's response was to clothe Himself in five garments of truth, which are the divine qualities that descend into engagement with evil. These are the "sons" or emanating powers of the Divine Rational, each truth serving as armor and instrument of combat.*

**¶15:** And at the time when evil propagated its own nature from its works through its successive offspring, they descended onto the plane of natural existence and [GAP-92] drew sustenance and strength from the fundamental evils and were nourished by them. [GAP-93] wickedness, together with cruelty [GAP-94] resided in the ruling self-love, the chief of all infernal spirits. He subjugated his realms and his subordinate powers; he gathered them all into himself. He made himself ready for the spiritual combat; he set himself to the war against that realm of divine wisdom, and the great King — the Lord Himself — who dwells within it. *That is: all hells were drawn under a single ruling evil — the love of dominion from self-love — which consolidated every falsity and every malice into one infernal will, directed against the Divine kingdom and the Lord who is its life.*

**¶16:** At that very moment the Divine Human drew near to His exterior truths — the celestial intelligences who radiate the Divine light. He communed with them, that He might entrust to them a [GAP-95] sacred charge; He [reve]aled to them and instructed them concerning everything that [GAP-96] pertained to them. He assumed these truths into Himself. He arranged them in order [GAP-97]. He clothed them one upon another over His own divine faculties [GAP-98] against the peril; it [GAP-99] the exalted states of the celestial realm [GAP-100] with all its powers [GAP-101: from the beg]inning, it being without measure or limit [GAP-102]. *That is: the Lord, preparing for the descent into temptation-combat, took upon Himself successive layers of truth — each garment corresponding to a degree of accommodation by which the Infinite could engage the finite hells. He ordered these truths from inmost to outmost upon His own being, each faculty clothed and armed, so that the Divine life — immeasurable in itself — could enter the field of spiritual warfare against the whole consolidated power of evil.*

---

*Note on method:* Throughout this translation, "the First Man" is read as the Divine Human — the Lord's own Rational proceeding into combat with the hells, which is Swedenborg's spiritual sense of every narrative in which a divine figure descends to engage evil. The five dark elements correspond to the five genera of infernal falsity and evil love. The five garments correspond to the five degrees of divine truth by which the Lord clothed Himself for the work of redemption. The "land" in every instance is a spiritual state, not a place.

fills.explanation: The pronoun "it" refers back to the subject introduced in the preceding large gap, denoting the divine substance or realm whose essence is being described.
The copular verb "is" completes the compound predicate: the essence both "is the land of X" and "is their last [boundary]," expressing that the realm encompasses both origin and uttermost extent.

Paragraph 2 describes the incomprehensible divine essence; "light" is the Kephalaia's standard term for the divine substance, and ¶3 then transitions to "the land of death" as the contrasting principle.
The editor's reconstruction fits the triadic disclosure formula (recount / unveil / say) and the spiritual sense of expressing the mode of the divine essence's existence.

fills.explanation: This is the standard Kephalaia eternity formula expressing infinite temporal extension in both directions, matching the spiritual sense of "throughout the infinite and eternal."
The verb "tend" takes the preposition "to" before its object: "tend to the beginning of eternity and the end" — pointing toward origin and boundary without being able to fully set them down.
Combined with the surviving "ver and ever," this restores the standard Kephalaia eternity formula "from ever for ever and ever," matching the spiritual sense of perpetual subsistence without end.

The participle "dwelling" bridges the eternity formula to the description of mutual opposition: "from ever for ever and ever, dwelling in strife with one another" — the dark essence perpetually abides in internal conflict.

The spiritual reading describes "the opposition of disorderly loves that feed upon one another"; "in strife with one another" is the natural Kephalaia expression for this mutual antagonism within the dark realm.

Paragraph 4 describes the inscrutable origin of the dark realm and its stirring against the light; "the darkness" is the standard Kephalaia designation for this principle, following the discussion of light's essence in ¶2.

The editor's "understand" correctly renders the inability of finite minds to grasp how the dark powers subsist; it fits the Kephalaia's expository register for describing the limits of created cognition.

The editor's "he kept" correctly describes the First Man's action of maintaining separation between darkness and the celestial kingdom, matching the spiritual sense of holding evil apart from divine order.
The definite article "the" before "darkness" is the standard Kephalaia construction; "mixed with the darkness" is the formulaic expression for the intermingling of the two principles.
The editor's "was" is confirmed; "the light was entwined with the darkness" uses the standard Coptic narrative past tense for describing the completed event of intermingling.
The conjunction "and" maintains the parallel structure: "the light was entwined with the darkness, and life in death" — mirroring the preceding pair "light mixed with darkness, and life with death."
The causal-temporal connector "For" opens the new paragraph in standard Kephalaia expository style, and "after it" introduces the temporal clause about darkness stirring in its own essence.
Completes "thought" (th + ought) and supplies the verb "arose"; the spiritual reading indicates "its intention and deliberate will arose within its own domain."
The definite article completes "For the essence in it," the standard Kephalaia construction for referring to the inmost nature of a principle.
The copula "is" introduces the description: "on its side is this first nature of it" — identifying the primal dark constitution whose body is then compared to the Adamant.
The preposition "of" creates the possessive "this first nature of it," designating the primal constitution of the dark principle whose body is then described as harder than adamant.
The intensifier "far" before the visible "more" strengthens the comparison: evil's corporeal form is made strong "far more than the Adamant," expressing its unyielding density.
The conjunction "and" extends the comparison: "far more than the Adamant and every thing" — the dark body surpasses both the hardest substance and everything else in the created order.
The generic noun "thing" completes the universal comparison: "every thing as it exists in the universe" — the dark body's strength surpasses all that exists in the whole created order.
The verb "fills" describes envy pervading the entire dark realm; the spiritual reading indicates envy as the consuming quality that characterizes the whole land of darkness.
The possessive "its" links the deliberation/consideration to the darkness's own wickedness: "consideration in its wickedness" describes evil's self-directed malicious intent.
Combined with the surviving "rom," this restores "forth from": "he will run forth from the land," describing the Divine Human's descent from the celestial realm into combat.
The preposition "of" completes "from the land of darkness," the standard Kephalaia designation for the realm into which the First Man descends.
The adverb "down" indicates the direction of darkness's action: "It drew down his members" — pulling the divine faculties into the infernal depths, matching the spiritual sense of descent.
The editor's phrase is confirmed; "the five dark elements" is the standard Kephalaia designation for the fundamental modes of evil, immediately enumerated as smoke, fire, wind, water, and Darkness.
The copula "are" introduces the enumeration of the five dark elements, confirmed by the editor and the spiritual reading.

The word "depths" locates evil's self-formation spatially within its own abyss, connecting forward to "the storehouses of its abyss" two lines later and to "the great depth" in ¶13, maintaining the consistent vertical imagery of evil consolidating itself in its own lowest regions before generating numerous emanations.
The preposition "in" is confirmed; "its birth in numerous emanations" describes evil propagating itself through innumerable derivative forms.
The preposition "in" is confirmed; "in the storehouses of its abyss" locates the dark creatures within the hidden repositories of the infernal depth.
The adjective "dark" is confirmed; "dark creatures" is the standard Kephalaia descriptor for beings generated from the five dark elements in the abyss.
The verb "spread" completes the triadic growth formula: "was established and spread and grew strong," describing evil's progressive consolidation and expansion through the dark realm.
The adjective "great" intensifies "impetuosity" in standard Kephalaia register: "by the great impetuosity" parallels the spiritual sense of the violence of their impulses.
The doublet "slaughter and devour" is the standard Manichaean/Kephalaia formula for the mutual destruction of the dark archons, who consume one another in perpetual internal warfare.
The ruler of darkness sensed the light existing above/beyond it; "light that is above it" matches the spiritual sense of perceiving divine wisdom that exists beyond the dark realm.
The darkness conspires against both the exalted kingdom and "the light" — the paired targets of infernal assault, paralleling ¶15's pairing of "that light earth and the great King."
The prepositional phrase "of the" connects the Father's knowledge to the coming war: "it also knew of the war," matching the spiritual sense that the Divine perceived the impending assault.
The editor's "land of" is confirmed; "the land of light" is the standard Kephalaia designation for the divine realm that darkness seeks to disturb.

The contrastive conjunction "but" marks the pivot from the threat (darkness disturbing the land of light) to the Father's wise counter-action: "to disturb the land of light, but in the wisdom of his greatness he transformed himself."
Combined with the surviving "-ness," this restores "greatness": "in the wisdom of his greatness" is the standard Kephalaia formula for the Father of Greatness acting through divine wisdom.
The connector "And" provides the standard paragraph transition, and "fr" combines with the surviving "om" to form "from": "And from its essence, poured it out in the elements."

The word "essence" is the chapter's recurring term for the inmost nature of a principle; "from its essence, poured it out" describes evil diffusing itself from its own inmost nature into the elements.
The editor's "great" is confirmed; "the great depth" is the standard Kephalaia expression for the immense abyss from which evil ascends.
The conjunction "and" links the two sequential actions of evil's self-propagation: "when it generated itself and it formed the fruits."

The verb "drew" describes evil's offspring extracting sustenance from the fundamental elements: "fell upon the earth and drew strength from the elements," matching the spiritual sense of drawing sustenance from the five evils.

The verb "dwell" describes how wickedness and cruelty reside in the ruling demon: "wickedness, together with cruelty, dwell in the ruler" — matching the spiritual sense that all evil was concentrated in the chief of the infernal powers.

In Kephalaia register, "mystery" is the standard term for sacred knowledge entrusted by a divine figure; the First Man entrusts a mystery to his garments before revealing and teaching them about the coming battle.

The phrase "would come upon" describes the First Man's prophetic revelation to his garments about everything that would befall them in the coming battle, a standard Kephalaia formula for divine foreknowledge shared before combat.
Combined with the surviving "inning," this restores "from the beginning": the darkness assembled all its powers from the beginning, its totality being immeasurable.
